subject: Qualification
notes: kb/Work PB919, wave 57. SR1 is now enforced for EVERY 8.4.2.2.2 qualified-name format through a named resolution each: data-name (QualifiedCandidates, counted by UniqueOrReportAmbiguous / ReportUnidentified), condition-name (ConditionBinder.ConditionOf), index-name (NEW: ReferenceResolver.ResolveIndexName over SymbolTable.IndexCandidates, counted by the same generic UniqueOrReportAmbiguous<T> verdict, COBOL1639), procedure-name (ResolveProcedureWord), LINAGE-COUNTER (LinageFileOf), LINE-/PAGE-COUNTER (CounterReportOf); screen-name is declared only by the DECLINED A.4.2 SCREEN SECTION. record-key-name (kb/Work PB1099, the SOURCE phrase provided from 2002): FileModel.RecordKeyNameCandidates answers a COUNTED set of KeyNameReading, and a position that admits data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 (READ/START KEY: KeyedIoBinder.RecordKeyNameOf; key-level COLLATING SEQUENCE: DataBinder.CollatingKeyNamed) counts every visible file's record-key-names AND every data-name reading (each same-spelled data item the written qualifiers reach: QualifiedCandidates, counted, never a unique-only probe) in that one set, judged by the same UniqueOrReportAmbiguous verdict (COBOL1639). Review R1-2 measured the alternative: a record-key-name declared by two clauses of one entry (no Format 6 qualifier can separate them) bound silently to the prime key (READ returned 23 reading the prime key), as did a name two files declare or a name also declared as a data-name (8.3.2.2 rule 3). QualifiedNameClassDriftTests derives the format list from the standard's own 8.4.2.2.2 text and fails on an unrouted format. Review R2-1 measured the probe it replaced: a probe answers only a UNIQUE data item, so one same-spelled data item made READ KEY IS RK ambiguous and a second one made it compile clean, bound silently to the record key; now both draw COBOL1639 (2 and 3 declarations; FileControlKeyRuleSpecTests.ARecordKeyNameReference_ThatQualificationLeavesNonUnique_IsSR1 rows DATA2). Before: index-names were keyed name -> cell, de-duplicated on insert, so two tables' INDEXED BY IX shared one cell and a bare IX compiled clean.
